# Keep tooltips within screen bounds

## Problem statement

Tooltips are rendered at a fixed offset from the hover point without any viewport-bounds checking. When a hovered element sits near the right or bottom edge of the window, the tooltip overflows the viewport; in the DOM-rendered mode this extends the document's scrollable area, so the page "resizes to make space" (scrollbars appear / layout shifts). The tooltip must always be positioned so that it is fully visible and never alters the document layout.

## Users

- **Players** hovering cards, HUD elements, and buttons in Main Street, Lost Cities, Sushi Go, and the Gym tooltip/Gym-card-index demos.
- **Engine consumers (game developers)** who rely on the shared `TooltipManager` (DOM and Phaser modes) so they do not have to re-implement bounds handling per game.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I hover a card near the right edge of the screen, the tooltip appears fully on-screen instead of being clipped or pushing the page wider.
- As a player, showing a tooltip never causes the game canvas or page to jump/resize.
- As a game developer, when I supply a `phaserRender` callback I can clamp my tooltip into the game canvas with a shared helper rather than copying clamp maths between games.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **DOM-mode clamping:** For a hover point near each of the four viewport edges, the DOM tooltip's rendered bounding rectangle is fully inside the browser viewport (`left >= 0`, `top >= 0`, `right <= window.innerWidth`, `bottom <= window.innerHeight`), with a small margin. Verified by a browser (`*.browser.test.ts`) test in `tests/ui/`.
2. **No document resize:** Showing (and hiding) a DOM tooltip does not change the document scroll size — no horizontal/vertical scrollbar is introduced (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` before and after `show()`). Verified by a browser test.
3. **Phaser-mode clamping:** The shared Phaser render callbacks keep their tooltip containers inside the game canvas bounds (`0..GAME_W` × `0..GAME_H`) at all four edges. Gym's callback (currently unclamped) is brought in line with the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, ideally via a shared, unit-tested helper. Verified by unit tests (helper) plus the existing scene/browser tests.
4. **No regression to existing positioning:** Existing world→screen coordinate mapping (canvas scale, canvas offset, camera scroll) and the settings `showTooltips` toggle behaviour are preserved; the existing `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` / `TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` expectations are updated rather than weakened.
5. **Validation and documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (tooltip component section) and any relevant Gym help text. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies.
- Must not regress reduced-motion, `pointer-events: none`, or the maximum `z-index` behaviour of the DOM tooltip.
- Must remain safe in non-DOM environments (`document`/`window` undefined) and when the canvas bounding rect cannot be read — fall back to hiding, as today.
- Clamping must be cheap (measure once per `show()`, no per-frame layout thrash, no resize listeners).
- The DOM tooltip node must not contribute to the document's scrollable overflow area.
- Use UK English in comments and docs; escape only backticks in worklog content.
- Existing tests that assert `div.style.position === 'absolute'` will need updating if the positioning strategy changes (see Risks).

## Existing state

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — `TooltipManager`. DOM mode computes `screenX`/`screenY` from the canvas rect, camera scroll, and scale, then sets `left`/`top` = point + `(10, 10)` offset with **no bounds check**. The node is `position: absolute`, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: 2147483647`, `max-width: 320px`, appended to `document.body`. Phaser mode delegates layout entirely to the caller's `phaserRender` callback.
- Consumers in DOM mode: Main Street (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` constructs it; `MainStreetRendererStreet/Hud/Market/Layout.ts` call `show`), `GymTooltipScene` DOM half, `GymCardIndexScene`.
- Consumers in Phaser mode: `LostCitiesScene.ts` (`createTooltipManager`) and `SushiGoScene.ts` — both already clamp with `Phaser.Math.Clamp(..., 4, GAME_W - boxW - 4)` etc. `GymTooltipScene`'s Phaser callback does **not** clamp.
- Tests: `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` (unit), `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` (browser, asserts `position === 'absolute'`), `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` (SLL anchors only), plus Main Street tooltip content tests.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents `TooltipManager`; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` maps the tooltip scenes.

## Desired change

- Add viewport-bounds clamping to the shared DOM tooltip renderer in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`:
  - Position the node relative to the viewport so it cannot extend the document scroll area (e.g. `position: fixed`).
  - Measure the node after setting content, then flip it above/left of the hover point when there is not enough room below/right, and clamp to the viewport as a final guard, keeping a small margin.
  - Keep the existing world→screen conversion (canvas rect + camera scroll + scale).
- Extract a reusable bounds-clamping helper for in-canvas (Phaser) tooltips, mirroring the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, and use it in `GymTooltipScene` (and optionally migrate Lost Cities / Sushi Go to the shared helper with no behaviour change).
- Add unit tests for the clamp maths (all four edges, both axes, oversized tooltip) and browser tests proving the tooltip stays in the viewport and does not change document scroll size.
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and Gym help text if the scene behaviour/description changes).
- **Test-first:** author the clamp-helper unit tests and the browser edge/document-scroll tests before wiring the DOM renderer and the Gym callback, so the new behaviour is specified by failing tests first.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — Add DOM-mode viewport clamping / anti-resize positioning; export a reusable Phaser-mode clamp helper.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — Apply the clamp helper in the `phaserRender` callback (currently unclamped).
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — Unit tests for clamp maths via the DOM mock and helper.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — Edge-position + document-scroll-size assertions; update the `position` selector assumption.
- `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` — Extend with Gym Phaser-mode in-bounds assertions (if the scene callback is changed).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the bounds guarantee for both tooltip modes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the correct, complete interpretation of the title is "no tooltip (in either DOM or Phaser mode) may render outside its visible bounds", not just the DOM overlay. The DOM mode is the cause of the reported page-resize; Phaser mode only clips. Recommended and assumed.
- **Assumption:** clamping (shift/flip to stay visible) is preferred over truncating content or shrinking the tooltip. Documented assumption; trivially revisitable.
- **Risk:** switching the DOM node to `position: fixed` invalidates the existing browser test's `position === 'absolute'` selector — update the selector to target the tooltip by its stable attributes (`pointer-events: none` + `z-index`) rather than `position`.
- **Risk:** measuring the node to clamp requires it to be laid out; setting `display: block` before measuring may cause a one-frame flash. Mitigate by measuring immediately after content is set and before paint (single synchronous reflow), or measure with `visibility: hidden` then reveal.
- **Risk:** `window`/`document` may be undefined in unit tests/SSR — guard clamping behind the existing `document` checks and fall back to the unclamped path (or hide) when dimensions are unavailable.
- **Risk:** double clamping when a game's `phaserRender` already clamps — the helper must be opt-in and not re-apply automatically to caller-managed containers.
- **Risk:** oversized tooltips (taller/wider than the viewport) cannot fit; clamp to the margin and accept partial visibility, documenting the behaviour.
- **Scope-creep risk:** tooltip content wrapping/truncation, touch/long-press tooltips, and tooltip theming are out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Related work

- **CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7** – Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover (completed) — introduced the shared `TooltipManager` this bug affects.
- **CG-0MODIX70W002JXQN** – `feat(ui): add TooltipManager` / `fix(ui): DOM-positioned tooltip displays above cards` — prior DOM coordinate-mapping work in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`.
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed) — SLL precedent for declarative positioning.
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed) — SLL layout system; relevant if bounds handling is expressed via SLL zones.
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed) — Main Street tooltip content fix, no overlap with positioning.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed)
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ake, bounds, displayed, ensure, keep (+11 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+10 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+7 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q:** Are there open questions requiring producer input? — **A:** No. The seed context ("Sometimes when a tooltip is displayed it would render outside the screen bounds. This results in the screen resizing to make space. We need to ensure that the tooltip is positioned such that it stays within screen bounds.") plus repository research was sufficient to draft a clear, testable brief. No interview round was required. Source: seed context supplied with the intake invocation + repo inspection.

**Prior related answers:** none.

**Research summary:** Inspected `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` (DOM node is `position: absolute` on `document.body` with no bounds check — the resize cause; Phaser mode delegates to `phaserRender`), the four in-repo consumers (Main Street, Gym DOM, Gym Phaser, Lost Cities, Sushi Go), and the existing tests/docs. Lost Cities and Sushi Go already clamp inside the canvas with `Phaser.Math.Clamp`; Gym and the DOM renderer do not. No existing shared clamp helper exists. Related completed tooltip work items were found via `wl search` (see automated report).

# Reputation and coins from Upcoming should flow in the correct direction

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Bug**

When an Upcoming card changes coins or reputation during the end-of-turn phased income presentation, the flow graphic must target the actor the effect is attached to: the affected **business card** when the effect is attached to a business, or the **HUD totals** when it is not — and in the direction that matches a gain (into the target) or a loss (out of the target). Today the phased `upcoming` phase is an unimplemented placeholder and always routes to a business grid, ignoring both attachment and reputation.

## Problem statement

In the end-of-turn phased income show (`base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → collect`), Upcoming-card coin/reputation effects do not animate to the correct actor or in the correct direction:

- `SlotPhaseBreakdown.upcomingDeltas` is a documented **placeholder that is always empty**, so the `upcoming` phase never shows Upcoming-card contributions.
- The `upcoming` case in `runIncomePhase` hard-codes a single source (the Upcoming panel, `{gameW * 0.5, queueTop}`) and a single target (the producing business's coin grid), so an effect that is **not attached to a business** is still drawn as a business-grid flow rather than a HUD-totals flow.
- The `upcoming`/`events` phases animate **coins only** — reputation changes are never animated.
- There is no per-delta attachment metadata on `SlotEventDelta` / `SlotPhaseBreakdown`, so the animation cannot distinguish business-attached effects (`EventCard.target` = `SpecificSynergy` / `RandomBusiness`) from unattached ones (`target` = `All`).

## Users & User Stories

- **Player** — "When an Upcoming card changes my coins or reputation at end of turn, I want the flying coins/pips to go *from the Upcoming card to the business it hit* (or to my HUD bank if it hits the bank), and to leave the business/bank when it is a loss, so I can tell at a glance who paid and who benefited."
- **Player (reduced motion / replay)** — "I still want the phase label and pacing to progress, but without any coin flights, and the turn must never be blocked or the state changed by the animation."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Business-attached routing.** When an Upcoming-card effect is attached to a business (source `EventCard.target` = `SpecificSynergy` or `RandomBusiness`), its coin **and** reputation flow animates between the Upcoming source and the affected business card (gain → lands on the card; loss → leaves the card). Verified by unit assertions on the flight start/end points and direction for both signs.
2. **Unattached routing.** When an Upcoming-card effect is not attached to a business (`target` = `All`), the flow animates between the Upcoming source and the **HUD totals** (coin counter for coins, reputation counter for reputation) and is not drawn via any business grid. Verified by unit assertions.
3. **Reputation parity.** Reputation deltas follow the same attachment and direction rules as coin deltas. Verified by unit assertions covering {gain, loss} × {attached, unattached}.
4. **Presentational only; accessibility preserved.** The change never mutates `state`, the transcript, or the turn flow, and does not alter credited coin/reputation totals; reduced-motion and replay/headless modes keep the existing no-flight exemption (phase labels still progress). Verified by the existing deferred-animator tests plus a new state-unchanged assertion.
5. **Tests and docs.** Task-targeted unit tests are added/updated (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/` passes) and `npm run build` succeeds. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (in particular `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`).
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Presentational only** (producer answer Q3 = A): the engine continues to apply deltas to `state.resourceBank`; only the VFX routing changes. Do **not** change where the economy is applied.
- Must not shorten the phase pacing (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS` / ≈11s collection) — an existing acceptance criterion of the phased-income feature.
- Must respect the reduced-motion preference and the replay/headless exemption (`scene.replayMode`) already used by the animator.
- Reuse existing infrastructure (`moveGameObject`, `SoundManager`, `popTextOrIcon`, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`); no new engine infrastructure or game-scoped SFX string literals.
- Any new phase data must be additive and must not change the existing credited totals or break the phase-sum invariant relied on by `creditedIncomeTotal`.
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` → `runIncomePhase`:
  - `'upcoming'` case flies `flyCoinsIn`/`flyCoinsOut` to/from each business grid from `{ x: s.layout.gameW * 0.5, y: s.layout.queueTop }`, iterating `slot.pd.upcomingDeltas`; no reputation handling.
  - `'events'` case routes per-slot `eventDeltas` from `animator.eventSourcePoint()` (the Upcoming panel effect line) to the business grid.
  - `'reputation'` case flies coins from the HUD reputation counter (`{ gameW * 0.5, hudY }`) into business grids.
- `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` → `SlotPhaseBreakdown.upcomingDeltas` is populated as `[]` everywhere (documented placeholder); `SlotEventDelta` carries `{ cardId, name, delta }` only (no attachment/target).
- Incident **resolution-time** deltas are separately animated HUD ↔ board-centre card by `MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` (`animateIncidentDeltaBubbles`), which already implements the gain/loss direction convention (`coinChange < 0` / `repChange < 0` → resource → card; positive → card → resource).
- `tests/main-street/income-phase-data.test.ts` asserts `upcomingDeltas` is currently always empty; `tests/main-street/income-phase-animation.browser.test.ts` and `income-phase-sequential-animator.test.ts` assert the phase order `base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → collect`.

## Desired change

1. Carry Upcoming-card coin **and** reputation deltas through the phase data, tagged by attachment: attached (business) vs unattached (HUD). Derive attachment from the source `EventCard.target` (`SpecificSynergy` / `RandomBusiness` = attached; `All` = HUD).
2. Populate `upcomingDeltas` (or an equivalent additive field) in the income/channel computation so the `upcoming` phase has real data, without changing the credited total or the phase-sum invariant.
3. Update `runIncomePhase` (`'upcoming'` and reputation handling) to route each delta to the affected **business grid** when attached or to the **HUD coin/reputation counter** when unattached, with the sign determining the direction. Reuse the existing HUD↔card direction convention from the incident animator.
4. Keep reduced-motion/replay as no-ops and preserve all pacing.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption (Q1 = A).** The fix lives on the **end-of-turn phased income animation** (`upcoming` / `reputation` / `events` phases).
- **Assumption (Q2 = A).** "Attached to a business" is determined by the source `EventCard.target` (`SpecificSynergy` / `RandomBusiness` = attached; `All` = HUD). Because Q2 describes one-off incident targets while the income phases consume per-slot income contributions, routing keys off the *source event's* `target` for any Upcoming-sourced delta in the phase data; where the phase data does not yet carry it, the implementer threads it through. If a cleaner existing signal (e.g. the active-effect source event) already encodes attachment, prefer it and document the choice.
- **Risk — missing metadata.** The phase data may not currently carry `target`; mitigation: thread the minimal metadata, or derive it from the source event, and cover it with a unit test.
- **Risk — invariant break.** Adding HUD-bound deltas to `upcomingDeltas` could break the phase-sum invariant / `creditedIncomeTotal`; mitigation: keep new data additive, do not change credited totals, and add a regression assertion.
- **Risk — incident-reveal regression.** The separate incident-reveal HUD↔card bubble path must not change; mitigation: treat `MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` as reference-only and add regression assertions.
- **Scope-creep risk.** A full redesign of incident resolution vs. income phases is out of scope; record any such opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `runIncomePhase` `'upcoming'` / `'reputation'` / `'events'` cases; add HUD-target flow routing; reuse `flyCoinsIn` / `flyCoinsOut`.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorContext.ts` — signatures for any new helpers/params.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `SlotEventDelta` / `SlotPhaseBreakdown` attachment metadata and `upcomingDeltas` population.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorUtils.ts` — `eventSourcePoint`, `creditedIncomeTotal`.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — reference for the HUD↔card direction convention (must not regress).
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — document the attachment/direction routing.
- `tests/main-street/income-phase-data.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/income-phase-animation.browser.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/income-phase-sequential-animator.test.ts` — tests.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** — Income Phase: phased card-effect animations (coin grids, synergy/rep/event contributions) — parent precedent; the `upcoming` phase originated here.
- **CG-0MTDEAA2J001EFEF** — Phased income animation (all phases, reduced motion) — AC6 explicitly requires "Upcoming cards affecting income fly coins in or out appropriately".
- **CG-0MU41XVNV002N2D9** — Resource-delta bubble animation — establishes the gain/loss HUD↔card direction convention reused here.
- **CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I** — Upcoming in end turn routine — the incident/Upcoming reveal surface.
- **CG-0MTV6LZEA003YS3E** — Synergy bonus coins animate along synergy lines — recent phase-routing precedent.
- **CG-0MTK2JHXD004KNQI** — End-of-turn VFX/SFX scaled to x100 — presentation scaling convention.
- **CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q** — Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end-of-turn cycle — deferred-mutation interaction the animator must not break.
- **CG-0MU40V8TG0024TOH** / **CG-0MTDE8GQP003ZITA** — `runIncomePhase` refactor and per-phase breakdown data model.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Which "Upcoming" presentation surface does this item cover?** — Answer (producer): **A — the end-of-turn phased income animation (`upcoming` / `reputation` / `events` phases).** Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2: What makes an Upcoming-card effect "attached to a business"?** — Answer (producer): **A — a one-off incident whose `EventCard.target` is `SpecificSynergy` or `RandomBusiness`.** Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3: Is this presentational only, and which direction convention applies?** — Answer (producer): **A — presentational only; delta still credits/debits the HUD resource bank; loss = resource → card, gain = card → resource; reduced-motion/replay keep the no-flight exemption.** Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MTDEEUWI0079IOV** – Tests + documentation (completed)
- **CG-0MMM3EX2E0VD02N0** – Easy mode: cannot buy in first round, end turn hangs (completed)
- **CG-0MQRA9QTA0012PNZ** – Generalize synergy bonus system to support per-card custom values (completed)

# Chore: Document config-driven game catalogue + create per-game build presets

## Problem statement

The config-driven game catalogue (`configs/*.json` presets + `GAMES_CONFIG`)
is only described briefly and in two places (README and the Developer Guide),
with no single authoritative reference covering the preset schema, resolution
order, the `GAME_INFO` convention, or how to author a new preset. The shipped
presets are distribution-oriented (`core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/`deluxe`/`full`);
none selects a *specific named game*, so a developer cannot build or run, for
example, Main Street in isolation from the launcher checkout.

## Users and user stories

- As a **game developer**, I want to build/run one specific game in isolation so
  I can iterate quickly without pulling in the other games, using
  `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id>`.
- As an **engine maintainer**, I want one authoritative document describing how
  build presets are structured, resolved and created, so I can add a preset
  correctly without reverse-engineering the plugin.
- As a **release engineer**, I want the README to keep a concise summary and
  link to the detailed doc, so the high-traffic entry point stays short while
  the full contract is discoverable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. README keeps a concise "Which games does a build include?" section and links
   to a dedicated detailed document (`docs/dev/game-configuration.md`) for full
   details, replacing the current `docs/DEVELOPER.md#config-driven-game-catalogue`
   anchor as the primary reference.
2. The detailed document describes the preset schema in full: the top-level
   `games` array; required `id`, `path`, `scenePath`; optional `adapterPath`,
   `siblingScenePath` and `siblingAdapterPath` (the `src/`-layout sibling
   fields, Option C); the non-schema `$comment` annotation; preset selection
   (`GAMES_CONFIG` preset name or explicit path, default `core-only`); the
   three-step resolution order (`<root>/<scenePath>` →
   `<path>/<siblingScenePath>` → `<path>/<scenePath>`); the always-present
   core-owned Gym; the `GAME_INFO` convention and parsing; and
   validation/failure modes. It explains what each shipped preset (distribution
   and per-game) is and how it is structured — not only one example.
3. A per-game preset exists at `configs/<game-id>.json` for every example game —
   `beleaguered-castle`, `blackjack`, `coloretto`, `feudalism`, `golf`,
   `lost-cities`, `main-street`, `sushi-go` — each containing exactly that one
   game entry (Gym is always added by the plugin).
4. `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id>` selects exactly that game (+ Gym): the generated
   registry for each per-game preset imports the game's scene class and no other
   game, and one representative per-game preset is verified with a real
   `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id> npm run build`.
5. Unit tests guard every per-game preset: each ships exactly one game, uses the
   sibling `../tce-<id>` path form, resolves to a real scene module with the
   expected scene class, and generates a catalogue containing that game + Gym and
   no other game. Existing distribution-preset and discovery-plugin tests still
   pass.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes: the README
   summary section, the `docs/DEVELOPER.md` catalogue section, the new
   `docs/dev/game-configuration.md`, `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`
   where it references `configs/*.json` presets, and the preset/`GAME_INFO`
   doc comment in `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` (which still lists
   the pre-rename preset names `core-only`, `all` and `sample`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not break the existing distribution presets (`core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/
  `deluxe`/`full`) or their tests; per-game presets are additive.

# Task: Create the nine `tce-*` GitHub repositories and push extracted history

## Goal

As a distribution maintainer I can clone each per-game repository
(`tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`,
`tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`) plus
`tableau-card-engine-core` from GitHub with `--recurse-submodules`, then run
`npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit`, and get a runnable
single-game TCE checkout — so the sibling-repo composition that F4/F9 built and
verified **locally** exists on the remote and is cloneable by anyone.

## Users (user stories)

- **Distribution maintainer** — creates the nine remotes **once**, in the final
  F9 Option C `src/` layout, so no history-rewriting re-push is ever needed.
- **Game developer** — `git clone --recurse-submodules
  git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tce-golf.git` and builds/tests the game against
  the engine pulled in as the `core` submodule.
- **Launcher / distribution builder** — composes a subset of the remote game
  repos as siblings (the `solo` and `full` presets) against fresh clones.

## Context

Split out of F4 (CG-0MTRO72W5003ECAK) per operator decision: F4 delivers the
local per-game launcher scaffold (configs, `GAME_INFO`, build/test/package,
history-preserving extraction); creating and pushing the remote repositories is
a separate concern. The F4 producer gate deferred remote creation until the F9
Option C `src/` layout settled, so the nine repos are created **once, in the
final `src/` shape** — no history-rewriting re-push.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The nine repositories exist on GitHub under `TheWizardsCode` at the remotes
   recorded in `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`:
   `tableau-card-engine-core`, `tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`,
   `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`,
   `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`.
2. Each repository's default branch contains the extracted,
   history-preserving tree in the F9 `src/` layout (extraction via
   `scripts/extract-repos.sh`, scaffold via `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`):
   the core repo holds the engine + Gym + launcher shell and **no games**; each
   game repo has its source at repo-root `src/` and wires the engine as a
   `core` git submodule pointing at
   `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core.git`.
3. From a **fresh remote clone**, `git clone --recurse-submodules <game-repo>`
   followed by `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm test -- --project unit`

4. The launcher can compose a subset of the **remote** repos as siblings (spot

5. Evidence is recorded on this work item: the extraction commit count per repo
   (as F1 did) and the source monorepo commit SHA the nine repos were extracted
   from.
6. No CI pipeline and no npm publication are added (out of scope, per the epic
   constraints).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. (In practice:
   `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 currently says the remotes are
   *not* created; `README.md`/`docs/DEVELOPER.md` clone guidance must document
   the `--recurse-submodules` workflow.)
8. Validation for the change: the extraction/scaffold unit suites
   (`tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts`,
   `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`) pass, and the published remotes
   are validated by the fresh-clone checks in AC3/AC4.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No CI pipeline and no npm publication (epic constraint).
- Never rewrite the source monorepo: extraction always operates on a clone
  (`git clone --no-local`); the monorepo `main` is never pushed to directly.
- `git filter-repo` is required and is **not currently installed** on this host
  (`pip install git-filter-repo` per
  `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`).
- GitHub org write access is required; the authenticated account
  (`SorraTheOrc`) is an **admin** of the `TheWizardsCode` org, so credentials are
  available and creating repos is permitted.
- Remotes use SSH (`git@github.com:...`), consistent with `repo-layout.json`.
- Repos are created once, after F9, in the final `src/` layout.
- **Visibility:** all nine repos are created **public** (producer answer, Q1).
- **Published refs:** push only `dev` plus `main` seeded from it; do **not**
  push the monorepo's feature/`wl-*` branches or its `v0.1.x` tags (Q4).
- **Source revision:** extract from the current `dev` HEAD and record its SHA
  as evidence (producer answer, Q3).

## Existing state

- **F1** delivered `scripts/extract-repos.sh` +
  `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` (history-preserving extraction; verified
  locally: 852 core commits, 23–995 per game).
- **F2** delivered the core-engine repo tree (locally verified standalone).

Extract all nine repos from the monorepo at the current `dev` HEAD, scaffold the

history to its default branch, and record the per-repo commit counts plus the
source SHA as evidence.

## Goal

Fix the shared `HandView` so that, when `maxSlots` is set, card and outline positions derive from the hand's **capacity** rather than the current card count — adding a card never moves an existing card or slot.

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Sibling test items add the failing unit and browser tests first.

Root cause: `computeCardPositions()` builds a row centred on `this.cards.length` (`layoutCardPositions({ count: this.cards.length, … })`), and `_computeOutlineSlots()` ghosts it (plus appending extras). The empty-hand branch already lays out the desired fixed `maxSlots` row, so that row is the template to reuse. `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path all re-derive the row/rotation normalisation from the occupied positions and must move to the template as well. `setMaxSlots()` currently only rebuilds outlines and does not re-lay the cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1–AC5: implement the capacity-template behaviour — outline slot positions identical for a hand of 0…`maxSlots` cards; `addCard` fills the next slot right of the occupied run while pre-existing card positions are unchanged; occupied outlines still match card `x/y/rotation` with extras below every card; `setMaxSlots(n)` is the only mutation that re-lays the row and always yields exactly `n` slots; the empty-hand capacity row is unchanged (same centred straight/arc row the cards will occupy).
- Add a shared private helper in `src/ui/HandView.ts` that derives the `maxSlots` template with the existing `layoutCardPositions` maths (gap = `spacing - cardWidth`, `centerX`, `maxWidth` compression, `arcRadius` Y) and the template-span rotation normalisation; recompute from current options on each use (no stale cache).
- `computeCardPositions()` horizontal returns the first `cards.length` template positions; over-capacity cards continue with the template step to the right (best-effort, no re-centring).
- `getInsertionPosition(index)` returns the template position at `index` (first `maxSlots`; template step beyond), so Market→hand transfer animations land exactly on the resting card.
- `_computeOutlineSlots()` derives all `count` slots from the same template (occupied slots ghost the card's **actual** sprite rotation, extras keep `depth = index - 0.5 - count`), replacing the per-count ghosting/extension branch.
- Rotation and arc normalisation in `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path use the template span when `maxSlots` is set, so per-card rotation is also stable across adds.
- `setMaxSlots(maxSlots)` re-lays the cards (calls `applyLayout()`), not just the outlines.
- Capacity-driven layout is keyed on `maxSlots !== undefined`, independent of `showPositionOutlines`; toggling outlines never moves cards.
- Hands without `maxSlots` keep the existing centred-on-count layout; vertical cascade keeps `baseY + i * spacing` and is not regressed.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` is reused unchanged.
- The sibling unit and browser test items pass (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `computeCardPositions()`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`, `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, `sortCards()` animated path, `setMaxSlots()`.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — reused to build the capacity row (no change expected).

**Deliverables:**

- Capacity-driven `HandView` layout with stable card and outline slots and green sibling tests.
